For the location section, I'd like to feature an image of a Hollywood mirror, which I'll send over shortly. We should include the full address of Fuel Rock Club, but I want to make sure the focus remains on our brand rather than just the venue itself. Let's frame the copy to say something like: "You'll find us at this venue, Fuel Rock Club, where we will be hosting our pop-up studio." Below that, we should list our dates and times, and include a call-to-action encouraging visitors to book online to guarantee a slot for their group and receive a free drink with their booking.

I don't want the Google reviews for Fuel Rock Club linked to the website. Instead, let's use a clean, static map graphic that doesn't link out to external reviews. On this map, I'd like to feature a prominent Spook Studio logo with an arrow pointing directly to the Fuel Rock Club location to keep the focus on our brand.

On the booking form, let's add a prominent, bold white title that reads: "Book Online to Receive a Complimentary Drink with Your Makeup Slot." Below that, include a brief note explaining group bookings: "Booking as a group? Simply select the same time slot as your friends so you can all get ready together." Finally, add a clear call to action: "Book now to avoid disappointment!"

For now, please keep this layout strictly text-based with no images. The mobile layout has some overlapping issues. First, the app header is clashing with the phone's status bar, causing the system icons (time, battery, and Wi-Fi) to overlap with our header. We need to adjust the header spacing to push it down. Additionally, the in-app voice feature is currently broken and needs to be fixed. Finally, the footer is too close to the bottom of the screen and needs a better margin. We should implement a global safe-area solution for both the header and footer to prevent them from overlapping with the device's system UI.

Regarding the side panel layout, the controls for "Pin to Taskbar", "Refresh", "Speak", "AI Reply", and "Pause" should be positioned underneath the "Polish", "Read Back", and "Send Now" buttons, as the current setup pushes content too far down the screen. Additionally, we don't need two redundant tabs specifying the active chat, since the spoken words section already indicates "sending to the chat." Instead, let's keep the active chat indicator next to the "AI Speak", "AI Reply", and "Pause" controls, and move "Refresh" and "Pin to Taskbar" to the footer to break up the layout better.
